title: Section 141 NI Act — Offences by companies

content.overview: Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 deals with offences by companies. If the s. 138 offence is committed by a company, every person who at the time of the offence was in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, as well as the company, shall be deemed guilty, subject to the defence that the offence was committed without that person's knowledge or that the person exercised all due diligence. Subsection (2) reaches a director, manager, secretary or other officer where the offence is committed with that person's consent or connivance, or is attributable to neglect on that person's part. The explanation includes a firm or other association of individuals within 'company', and a partner within 'director'.
content.study: Plead the company and the role. The statutory test in subsection (1) is 'in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of the business', not the mere title of director. Subsection (2) is a separate consent, connivance or neglect route and needs its own averment. A firm is a company for this section, and a partner is a director for this section.

learningObjectives: Apply the deemed-guilt rule in s. 141(1) to the company and persons in charge.
State the knowledge and due-diligence defence.
Separate s. 141(2) consent, connivance or neglect from the subsection (1) test.
enhancement.definition: Section 141 deems the company, and every person then in charge of and responsible for the conduct of its business, guilty of a s. 138 offence, with a stated defence, and adds a consent, connivance or neglect route for officers.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Vicarious liability under s. 141 is statutory and averment-specific. Designation alone is not the subsection (1) test. The company remains an accused.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, s. 141, explanation, read with s. 138. Cognizance of the resulting complaint remains s. 142.
essentialIngredients: Section 138 offence committed by a company
Person was at that time in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business, or
Director, manager, secretary or other officer with consent, connivance or attributable neglect
Defence: no knowledge, or all due diligence to prevent the offence
Firm treated as company; partner treated as director
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 141(1) has two accused classes: the company, and every person who, when the offence was committed, was in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business. Both limbs of that personal test matter. The proviso lets such a person escape liability by proving lack of knowledge or exercise of all due diligence. Section 141(2) is not a restatement of subsection (1). It applies where the offence is committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to neglect on the part of, a director, manager, secretary or other officer, and that person is also deemed guilty. A complaint that only says 'director' without an in-charge-and-responsible averment, and without a subsection (2) consent or neglect averment, does not meet the statutory text. The explanation prevents a firm from being left outside the section. This note does not adopt a judicial holding on whether the company must be arraigned before an officer; that point stays on the case-law gate.
examples: A private company issues the cheque. The complaint names the company and the managing director with a specific in-charge-and-responsible averment.
A nominee director is named with no averment of being in charge or of consent, connivance or neglect. The statutory tests are not pleaded.
A partner of a firm signs the firm's cheque. The explanation treats the firm as a company and the partner as a director for s. 141.
An officer proves the cheque was issued without that officer's knowledge and despite due diligence systems. That is the subsection (1) proviso defence.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the drawer entity. If it is a company or firm, name it. For each natural person, choose subsection (1) or (2) and plead the matching words. Do not use s. 139 to supply the role averment.
distinctions: Section 141(1) in-charge test vs s. 141(2) consent or neglect
Director by title vs person in charge of and responsible for the business

keyTakeaways: The company is deemed guilty along with persons in charge.
In charge of and responsible is the subsection (1) test.
Lack of knowledge or due diligence is a statutory defence.
Consent, connivance or neglect is a separate subsection (2) route.
A firm is a company and a partner is a director for this section.
